No supporting or refuting evidence is attached to this hypothesis; nothing in the record contradicts the stated actor, place, mechanism, or interval.

The single refuting citation (boslough-2012-chapter-c0) argues against the physical plausibility of a cosmic impact (no crater, no chondritic geochemistry, no adequate airburst cooling mechanism), but it does not address 'independent-replication-failure' specifically, nor does it place the actor/object outside North America or outside the -10950 interval. It critiques the impact hypothesis on different grounds than the mechanism asserted here, so it is not a concrete contradiction of this specific placement's actor, place, or interval.

The cited evidence (buchanan-2008-c0, holliday-2014-synthesis-c0, holliday-meltzer-2010-c0) reports no Paleoindian population decline or collapse at 12.9 ka in North America, which is consistent with -- not contradictory to -- the hypothesis's claim that a cosmic-impact effect on population-demography via gamma-ray-ionization is 'refuted'. The evidence matches the stated place (North America) and interval (~12.9 ka), so there is no concrete contradiction of this placement.
